machine.name: Dr. Dude And His Excellent Ray (WPC)

mechanisms.behavior: An outhole contact 22 detects the drained ball; output 9 drives its kicker. Three trough contacts 23, 24 and 25 detect the queued balls; output 10 drives the shooter-lane feeder. The WPC change sheet lists replacement outhole and feeder assemblies. Exact ball-path timing and jam behavior require prototype evidence. The common physical assembly establishes moving parts, while implementation speed and geometry are table-owned. Do not synthesize a feedback switch absent from its sensor list.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball trough and outhole

mechanisms.behavior: A manual spring shooter launches from the shooter lane detected by switch 21. No automatic shooter coil is declared in the WPC table. Simulator output 49 is an emulator shooter-release state, not a physical actuator. The common physical assembly establishes moving parts, while implementation speed and geometry are table-owned. Do not synthesize a feedback switch absent from its sensor list.
mechanisms.label: Manual shooter

mechanisms.behavior: The top-left popper has switch 73 and output 1. Factory table names its coil and the shared manual describes the mechanical assembly; prototype-specific stroke timing and ball route remain candidate. The common physical assembly establishes moving parts, while implementation speed and geometry are table-owned. Do not synthesize a feedback switch absent from its sensor list.
mechanisms.label: Top left popper

mechanisms.behavior: The middle-right popper has switch 48 and output 2. Factory table names its coil and the shared manual describes the mechanical assembly; prototype-specific stroke timing and ball route remain candidate. The common physical assembly establishes moving parts, while implementation speed and geometry are table-owned. Do not synthesize a feedback switch absent from its sensor list.
mechanisms.label: Middle right popper

mechanisms.behavior: The right four-target bank uses switches 35 through 38, ordered top to bottom. Output 4 drives the reset assembly. The retained common assembly documentation shows a four-target bank; startup and reset timing require prototype-specific proof. The common physical assembly establishes moving parts, while implementation speed and geometry are table-owned. Do not synthesize a feedback switch absent from its sensor list.
mechanisms.label: Four-target drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 72 is the Magnetic Personality target; output 5 drives the magnet. No magnet home or ball-presence sensor is established. The relation between target and field is spatial, not direct actuation. The common physical assembly establishes moving parts, while implementation speed and geometry are table-owned. Do not synthesize a feedback switch absent from its sensor list.
mechanisms.label: Magnet

mechanisms.behavior: The raised Mixmaster uses ramp entrance 27 and made switch 28 and has nine target switches 51–56 and 61–63. Output 27 drives the motor. Shared factory parts documentation describes the common mechanism; WPC-specific operating timing, home state and jam behavior require further evidence. The common physical assembly establishes moving parts, while implementation speed and geometry are table-owned. Do not synthesize a feedback switch absent from its sensor list.
mechanisms.label: Molecular Mixmaster

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 47 is the Big Shot target; output 3 drives its kicker and character linkage. The WPC table names the coil. No additional position sensor or prototype-specific motion timing is established. The common physical assembly establishes moving parts, while implementation speed and geometry are table-owned. Do not synthesize a feedback switch absent from its sensor list.
mechanisms.label: Big Shot
